newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE GRAINS UP ON STG, SPREADS LIFT BARLEY VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE GRAINS UP ON STG, SPREADS LIFT BARLEY VOLUME.

text.p: LIFFE grains moved higher as sterling's dive put shorts under pressure to buy, traders said.
Good volume, notably on barley, was helped by spread trading between wheat and barley at around five stg, one trader said. November/November spreading featured in particular, he said.
It helped drive barley volume up to an unusually high 277 lots. "It's nice to see 277 lots on barley. Normally these days we don't see that in a week," the trader said.
A lack of farmer selling remained an inhibiting factor, particularly on wheat, where intermittent rain has meant a slow harvest.
On wheat, active November last traded 1.15 stg up at 85.65 stg. November volume was 185 of the total 445 lots.
On barley November was also the most active contract, moving 1.20 stg higher to 80.75 stg on volume of 111 of the total 277 lots.
Sterling/mark stood at 3.0013/23 in late European trade, compared with a session high of 3.0548 marks.
"Watch the currency, that is going to be the first infuence in the morning for sure," the trader said.
